author: Zoe Tillman, Chris Strohm, Hadriana Lowenkron
description: Victims of so-called government weaponization could seek money from the proposed fund.
title: Trump’s IRS Suit May End With a $1.7 Billion Compensation Fund

description:
For generations, Martin's Tavern in Georgetown has been a gathering place for presidents, lawmakers, journalists and insiders. And last weekend, it got a fresh national spotlight, when Saturday Night Live opened its show with a shot of the DC institution. Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power" host Joe Mathieu spoke with owner Billy Martin - the fourth Billy Martin to own and operate the restaurant - about its history and its staying power.

 (Source: Bloomberg)
title: DC Landmark Gets The ‘SNL’ Treatment

description: Christopher Smart, Managing Partner and Founder of the Arbroath Group, says incoming Fed Chair Kevin Warsh cannot "credibly" argue for rate cuts "at this stage," as energy prices surge and inflation pressures build. He says the Trump-Xi summit was "good symbolically" but warns investors should be "particularly skeptical" of US trade announcements China does not confirm. Smart also says trading by the president and members of Congress undermines "credibility in markets" and government. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Warsh Can't Push Cuts 'At This Stage:' Christopher Smart

author: Greg Stohr
description: The US Supreme Court rejected a last-ditch bid by Virginia Democrats to revive a voter-approved map that was designed to flip four Republican-held US House seats in the November election.
title: Supreme Court Rejects Virginia Democrats on Reviving Voting Map

description: Senator Chris Coons (D-DE), who serves on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee and Senate Appropriations Committee, says President Trump went to China on "a weaker footing" and warns his silence on Taiwan arms sales was "a critical step backwards" for US interests. He says China learned from the Strait of Hormuz closure that a blockade is "an incredibly powerful tool" and sees "no reason" to believe Xi Jinping will help pressure Iran to reopen the strait to other countries' ships. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's Balance of Power. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Took 'Critical Step Backwards' on Taiwan: Sen. Coons

author: Thomas Seal, Katie Greifeld
description: Enbridge Inc. “definitely would consider” backing a new oil pipeline to Canada’s west coast, its chief executive officer said, giving an early vote of confidence hours after Prime Minister Mark Carney signed an energy deal with Alberta Premier Danielle Smith.
title: Enbridge Warms Up to New Canada Oil Pipeline After Carbon Compromise

author: K Oanh Ha, Yang Yang (News), Rachael Lewis-Krisky
description: On today’s Big Take podcast: President Trump’s summit with Xi Jinping offered good optics, but gave little indication of progress on major sticking points.
title: From Trade to Taiwan, What the Trump-Xi Summit Did (and Didn’t) Accomplish

description: Today, Tyler Kendall wraps up Trump's summit with China's Xi Jinping from Beijing. Then, Priya Misra and Marta Norton break down the geoeconomics landscape as oil prices push bond yields higher and spark a stock selloff. Plus, Brad Stone talks his profile of Amazon CEO Andy Jassy and the big bets the company is making on AI. Finally, Blake Leonard, discusses consumer trends in the beverage market and how her family is keeping costs low for shoppers. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Oil Prices Spook Investors, Consumers Feel Price Crunch | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 5/15/2026

author: Nathan R Dean
description: The agriculture industry has been hit by higher costs, declining exports
title: US Farmers Hoping the Trump-Xi Summit Will Lift Sagging Fortunes

author: Patrick Gillespie
description: State-run Argentine energy giant YPF SA announced a $25 billion project to accelerate oil production in the country, marking the largest investment since President Javier Milei took office.
title: Argentina’s YPF Seeks Incentives for $25 Billion Oil Project

author: Alicia A. Caldwell
description: Migrant arrests at the US-Mexico border edged up to the most in President Donald Trump’s second term after plunging when he returned to office in January 2025.
title: Border Arrests Rise for Third Straight Month to Most Under Trump

description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz discuss the conclusion of President Trump's trip to China. On today's show, Republican Congressman Vince Fong, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Third Way Executive Vice President Jim Kessler and former Fed Vice Chair Lael Brainard. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Wraps Up China Trip | Balance of Power: Early Edition 5/15/2026

author: Rachel Cohrs Zhang
description: A key ally of former Food and Drug Administration commissioner Marty Makary is departing the agency, according to people familiar with the matter. It’s expected to be the first in a series of changes the Trump administration will make to create a clean slate at the agency.
title: FDA Revamp Begins With the Departure of a Marty Makary Ally

author: Daniel Carvalho
description: Brazil’s top court ordered the arrest of the head of a private refining group in the latest effort to crack down on organized crime infiltrating in the formal economy.
title: Rio de Janeiro Fuel Fraud Probe Sweeps Up Head of Refining Group

author: Eric Martin
description: Israel and Lebanon agreed to extend a ceasefire for 45 days to allow for more talks, the US State Department said on Friday, as the Trump administration tries to tamp down a conflict that’s made ending the war against Iran more difficult.
title: Israel, Lebanon Extend Ceasefire 45 Days After Washington Talks

author: Ilena Peng
description: China has renewed export licenses for 425 US beef plants, making way for a full resumption of trade for the protein between the two countries, according to the US Meat Export Federation.
title: China Allows Exports for 425 US Beef Plants, Trade Group Says

author: Skylar Woodhouse, Jeff Mason, Josh Wingrove
description: China called for a rapid reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, a goal it shares with the US, though there was no sign of a breakthrough between the superpowers on how to achieve that after President Donald Trump’s trip to Beijing.
title: Trump, Xi Project Hormuz Alignment Despite Lack of Iran Progress

author: Jennifer A Dlouhy
description: The Trump administration plans to streamline the permitting process for oil developments inside the National Petroleum Reserve-Alaska as it pushes to accelerate crude production in the US Arctic.
title: Trump Administration Pushes to Speed Oil Permitting in Alaska

description: Today marks the end of Jerome Powell's term as Fed Chair. His tenure will be defined by the pandemic and his response to the inflation surge that followed. Lael Brainard, Former Director of the National Economic Council During the Biden Administration, Former Vice Chair of the Federal Reserve, Distinguished Fellow at the Georgetown Psaros Center for Financial Markets and Policy joins to discuss the future of the Fed and Kevin Warsh's Chairmanship.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Fed Faces Regime Change as Powell's Steps Down as Chair

author: Michael O'Boyle
description: Mexican financial authorities blocked the bank accounts of the governor of Sinaloa state and nine other current and former officials who are facing US charges that they aided drug traffickers.
title: Mexico Blocks Bank Accounts of Governor Facing US Drug Charges

author: Alex Wickham
description: Investors are bracing for a period of instability as a protracted Labour party leadership contest looms
title: How Keir Starmer Imploded and Plunged Britain Into More Chaos

author: Bob Van Voris
description: The US charged an Iraqi national with participating in terrorist attacks against US targets, including a planned synagogue bombing in New York and the European offices of two American banks.
title: Iran-Linked Militant Plotted Attacks in US and Europe, DOJ Says

author: Alaric Nightingale
description: A Russian court ordered the Euroclear Ltd. clearinghouse to pay €200 billion ($233 billion) to the nation’s central bank, according to the Interfax news service, in a suit related to the European Union’s freeze of Russian assets.
title: Russia Orders Euroclear to Pay €200 Billion to Central Bank

description:
These are the Labour contenders who could unseat UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer.

Alex Morgan explains what they might mean for markets. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: The Labour Contenders Who Could Replace Starmer

description: President Donald Trump says didn't ask Xi Jinping for any favors when it comes to Iran. He says Xi largely agrees with him on the risks of Iran becoming a nuclear power. But Trump says he didn't ask the Chinese leader to put any pressure on Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Says He Didn't Ask Xi For Any Favors on Iran

author: Olga Kharif, Lydia Beyoud
description: For years, big banks worked to keep crypto out of mainstream finance, citing everything from money laundering and fraud to stability risks, and arguing the industry could not enjoy bank-like privileges without bank-equivalent oversight.
title: Crypto’s Win on Landmark Legislation Reshapes Rivalry With Banks

author: Jim Wyss
description: Las empresas privadas que surgieron en la isla a pesar de años de persecución serán fundamentales para lo que venga, ahora que Trump presiona para poner fin a 67 años de régimen unipartidista.
title: Los capitalistas de Cuba podrían ser la solución para la isla tras escasez de petróleo

author: Felipe Saturnino, Daniela Milanese
description: Analysts are underestimating the chances that a right-wing candidate other than Senator Flavio Bolsonaro reaches Brazil’s runoff election against President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, according to Eurasia Group.
title: Eurasia Sees Rising Odds of Right-Wing Surprise in Brazil Vote

author: Gabrielle Coppola
description: Hyundai Motor Group’s top US lobbyist is leaving his role after a year on the job, a significant departure as the automaker contends with punishing tariffs and unpredictable policy swings under President Donald Trump.
title: Hyundai’s Top US Lobbyist to Depart After One Year in Key Role

description: The British pound is heading for its worst week since 2024 against the US dollar and gilt yields surged as the pressure on UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer keeps building. Labour's Andy Burnham could try to get back to Westminster and make a run at Starmer. Bloomberg's Lizzy Burden has the latest from 10 Downing Street on "Bloomberg Brief." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Pound and Gilts Under Pressure Amid Starmer Uncertainty

author: Sudhi Ranjan Sen, Rakesh Sharma
description: India is examining the circumstances of an attack on a cargo vessel that caught fire before sinking in the Gulf of Oman, according to officials familiar with the matter.
title: India Seeks to Verify Details of Ship Attack in Gulf of Oman

author: Foster Wong
description: China’s Ministry of Justice said the European Union’s use of its foreign subsidies regulation in a probe of Chinese security firm Nuctech Co. constitutes improper extraterritorial jurisdiction and barred compliance with the measures.
title: China Criticizes EU Over Improper Jurisdiction in Nuctech Probe

author: Jim Wyss
description: Private businesses that emerged on the island despite years of persecution will be key to whatever comes next as Trump pushes to end 67 years of one-party rule.
title: Communist Cuba Is Leaning on Capitalists After Oil Runs Out

author: Zach C Cohen
description: House Republicans will likely forfeit their chance to pass another partisan fiscal package ahead of the midterm elections if they don’t wrap up their work before the August recess, a member of that chamber’s leadership team said Friday.
title: Third GOP Megabill Could Slip Until After Elections, Moore Says

description: President Donald Trump says the US made great trade deals with China during his meeting with Xi Jinping. He says China will buy over 200 planes from Boeing and possibly 750 more, but he provided no specifics. Trump also said China is buying engines from General Electric. He spoke to reporters on Air Force One Friday. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Says China Will Buy Over 200 Boeing Planes

author: Selcan Hacaoglu, Firat Kozok
description: Turkey has proposed building a $1.2 billion (€1 billion) fuel pipeline for military use to help meet the energy needs of allies on NATO’s eastern European flank, according to people familiar with the matter.
title: Turkey Floats $1.2 Billion Fuel Pipeline to Eastern NATO Allies

author: Rakesh Sharma
description: India will partner with the United Arab Emirates to expand its strategic crude and gas reserves, a key step for the world’s third-largest oil consumer to guard against future supply disruptions.
title: Modi Agrees With UAE to Build Strategic Crude, Gas Stockpiles

description: US President Donald Trump says he discussed guardrails on artificial intelligence with Chinese leader Xi Jinping during a two-day summit in Beijing. Trump spoke to reporters in Air Force One Friday after leaving China.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Says He Spoke to Xi About Guardrails for AI

author: Skylar Woodhouse, Jeff Mason
description: President Donald Trump said he’s weighing whether to ease sanctions on Chinese oil companies that buy supplies from Iran, a move that would mark a concession to Beijing after his summit with President Xi Jinping.
title: Trump Says He May Remove Some Iran-Linked Sanctions on China

author: Fabiola Zerpa, Nicolle Yapur, Todd Gillespie
description: Peter Thiel-backed startup Erebor Bank has pitched itself to top Venezuelan officials on restoring the sanctioned country’s access to the US financial system, an unexpected play by a new firm that’s stepping into a politically sensitive market many global banks still avoid.
title: Thiel-Backed Erebor Offers Venezuela Unlikely Banking Lifeline

author: Weilun Soon, Alex Longley
description: Iran seized a Chinese-owned ship that’s one of a handful of so-called floating armories that operate in the region, according to two maritime security consultants who asked not to be identified discussing sensitive information.
title: Iran’s Latest Ship Seizure Is a Chinese-Owned Floating Armory

author: Charlie Zhu, Jing Li, Colum Murphy, Rebecca Choong Wilkins
description: Before Donald Trump had even wrapped his two days of summitry and sightseeing in Beijing, Xi Jinping declared the visit a “historic” landmark in US-China ties despite the absence of any major deals or obvious breakthroughs.
title: Emboldened Xi Moves to Corner Trump With ‘New Relationship’ Talk

author: Alex Morales
description: The UK government has banned 11 foreign far-right agitators from entering the country ahead of a planned Unite the Kingdom march on Saturday orchestrated by Tommy Robinson.
title: UK Bars Foreign Far-Right Agitators Ahead of London Protest

author: Firat Kozok, Selcan Hacaoglu
description: President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s ruling AK Party is seeking to give him the power to declare an exclusive economic zone extending as far as 200 nautical miles (370 kilometers) from Turkey’s coast, according to people familiar with the matter.
title: Turkey Seeks to Assert Erdogan’s Power Over Contested Waters

description: US President Donald Trump said he made no commitment to Chinese leader Xi Jinping over Taiwan, and said he would make a decision soon over a planned $14 billion arms deal with the island. Trump’s remarks aboard Air Force One came after Xi issued an unusually blunt warning that the two nations could descend into conflict if the Taiwan issue is mismanaged. Bloomberg's Annmarie Hordern reports from Beijing. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Says He Made No Commitment to Xi Over Taiwan

description: Pomp, toasts and Taiwan — US President Donald Trump and China's Xi Jinping met this week for a two-day summit in Beijing. Jeff Mason followed the action on the ground and caught a glimpse of how it unfolded. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: How Trump's Visit to China for a Summit with Xi Unfolded

author: Josh Wingrove
description: President Donald Trump said China’s Xi Jinping largely agrees with him on the risks of Iran becoming a nuclear power but said he did not push his Chinese counterpart to pressure Tehran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
title: Trump Says He Didn’t Ask Xi to Pressure Iran on Strait of Hormuz

author: Courtney Subramanian
description: US President Donald Trump said he did not discuss a possible extension of his tariff truce when he met with Chinese leader Xi Jinping during a summit in China.
title: Trump Says He Didn’t Discuss Extending Tariff Truce With Xi

author: Michael Shepard
description: US President Donald Trump said he discussed guardrails on artificial intelligence with Chinese leader Xi Jinping, while adding that Nvidia Corp.’s H200 chips also came up during a two-day summit in Beijing.
title: Trump Says He Discussed AI Guardrails, Nvidia’s Chips With Xi

author: Sudhi Ranjan Sen
description: BRICS foreign ministers failed to reach a consensus at a meeting hosted by India, exposing deep divisions within the bloc over the conflict in Iran.
title: India Fails to Bridge Divide Over Iran War at BRICS Summit

author: Jonathan Tamari
description: Governors are increasingly taking the lead on the No. 1 election issue
title: States Spearhead Affordability Plans as Washington Stumbles

author: Joe Mayes
description: If Angela Rayner succeeds Keir Starmer as Britain’s next prime minister, it will complete a remarkable political ascent to the top job by the self-described “proper working-class woman.”
title: Rayner Shows She’s Force in UK No Matter How PM Fight Shakes Out

author: Michael Tighe
description: China promised Boeing Co. it will purchase 750 planes and also said it will buy as many as 450 General Electric Co. engines, US President Donald Trump said.
title: Trump Says China Promised to Buy More Boeing Planes, GE Engines

author: Ben Sills
description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said that he wouldn’t recommend his children go to live in the US because of what he described as a “social climate” that has suddenly taken hold.
title: Germany’s Merz Says He Wouldn’t Advise His Children Work in US

description: Nicholas Burns, former US Ambassador to China, joins Bloomberg’s Vonnie Quinn on “Bloomberg Brief” to discuss US-China relations as President Donald Trump and President Xi Jinping wrap up a two-day summit in Beijing. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Burns on Key Takeaways From the Trump-Xi Summit

author: Courtney Subramanian, Skylar Woodhouse
description: US President Donald Trump said he made no commitment to Chinese President Xi Jinping over Taiwan, and would make a decision soon over a $14 billion arms deal with the island.
title: Trump Says He Was Noncommittal on Taiwan, to Decide on Sale Soon

author: Milda Seputyte
description: The US has too much at stake in Europe to exit the NATO defense alliance and its own vested interests will dictate a continued presence on the continent, according to Finnish President Alexander Stubb.
title: US Needs NATO to Counter Russian Nukes, Finland’s Stubb Says

author: Andras Gergely
description: Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar is opening Viktor Orban’s offices to the public to dismantle the symbols of his predecessor’s rule as part of efforts to tackle costly building projects around Buda castle.
title: Magyar Opens Orban’s Office to Unpick Hungary’s Illiberal Legacy

author: Steven T. Dennis
description: The Republican-led Congress, faced with deepening economic discontent exacerbated by President Donald Trump’s Iran war, is struggling to find consensus on any plan to address the cost of living with less than six months before midterm elections.
title: Republicans Fumble on Affordability as Voters’ Worries Mount

author: Lucy White
description: Labour’s Andy Burnham is set to face off with Nigel Farage’s right-wing Reform UK as he attempts to win a seat in the House of Commons, a prerequisite for challenging Keir Starmer to achieve his ambition of becoming the UK’s next prime minister.
title: Burnham Faces Showdown With Farage Before He Can Get to Starmer

author: Flavia Krause-Jackson
description: Starmer’s premiership at risk as traditional two-party UK political system shatters.
title: UK Shows Few Leaders Last in Ungovernable Era

author: Jeff Mason, Skylar Woodhouse
description: Donald Trump got the pageantry he craved during his trip to China. But the US president concluded the summit largely where he began, receiving little help from his “friend” Xi Jinping in dealing with a messy war in Iran and a challenging political climate at home.
title: Winners and Losers From Trump and Xi’s Two-Day Beijing Summit

author: Skylar Woodhouse
description: President Donald Trump said he would install his proposed sculpture garden of “American Heroes” in West Potomac Park, a stretch near the National Mall that includes the Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial.
title: Trump Announces Plans For Statue Garden in Potomac River Park

author: Sam Dagher, Fiona MacDonald
description: The United Arab Emirates tried to persuade neighboring states including Saudi Arabia and Qatar to take part in a coordinated military response to Iran’s strikes and was left frustrated when they refused, according to people familiar with the matter.
title: UAE Tried in Vain to Get Saudis to Coordinate on Iran Response

description: US President Donald Trump's two-day visit to China has come to an end. President Xi Jinping hailed the results of the summit and touted an agreement on a new relationship for the countries, projecting optimism despite unresolved tensions and limited deals announced so far.  Bloomberg's Minmin Low reports from Beijing. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Xi Hails ‘Landmark’ Summit as Trump Departs

description: US President Donald Trump's two-day visit to China has come to an end. President Xi Jinping said the two nations agreed to stabilize trade relations. Bloomberg's Brendan Murray recaps the summit and what key issues were discussed by the leaders. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump-Xi Summit: What Was Discussed

author: Nariman Gizitdinov
description: Kazakhstan’s President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev is looking to secure his legacy by backing a new political party in the latest move to overhaul the country’s political system.
title: Kazakhstan’s New Adilet Party Seeks to Secure Tokayev’s Power Revamp

author: Greg Ritchie, James Hirai
description: Gilts tumbled after Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham secured a pathway to potentially challenge Keir Starmer for the UK prime minister’s job, threatening a fresh bout of political instability that investors fear could result in more expansive fiscal policy.
title: Gilts Slump as Investors Brace for Burnham Challenge to Starmer

author: Tooba Khan, Stephen Stapczynski
description: Pakistan has imported its second shipment of liquefied natural gas from the Persian Gulf in a week, showing how Islamabad is leveraging its newfound geopolitical influence to ease an energy crunch.
title: Pakistan Uses Newfound Diplomatic Clout to Get Persian Gulf LNG

author: Skylar Woodhouse, Omar Tamo
description: President Donald Trump said the US and China share common goals for ending the Iran war, while Beijing struck a measured tone in urging further diplomacy.
title: Trump Projects Confidence on Iran War While China Stays Cautious

author: Kirsi Heikel
description: Finland warned the public of drones possibly entering its airspace, for the first time near Helsinki, in the early hours of Friday.
title: Finland’s First Drone Scare Near Helsinki Disrupts Flights

description: Hetal Mehta, chief economist at St. James's Place, comments on the UK fiscal situation and gilt market reaction as pressure on Keir Starmer mounts following moves by senior Labour Party rivals to potentially challenge him as prime minister. Mehta tells Bloomberg Television that a more left-leaning leader raises the prospect of higher spending and higher taxes, which gets "into a territory where you disincentivize economic activity." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Labour Power Struggle Highlights UK Fiscal Dilemma

author: Netty Idayu Ismail
description: Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said Malaysia won’t consider any pardon request involving Jho Low, the alleged mastermind behind the multibillion-dollar 1MDB scandal who is seeking clemency from US President Donald Trump, Bernama reported.
title: Anwar Won’t Pardon Jho Low as 1MDB Fugitive Seeks Clemency in US

description: Mayor of Manchester Andy Burnham secured a path to challenge Keir Starmer for the UK prime minister’s job, after a Labour Party Member of Parliament quit his seat in the House of Commons. Burnham said he would seek permission from Labour’s National Executive Committee to run for the freed-up seat in a by-election. Bloomberg's Alex Morgan reports from Downing Street. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Burnham's Move Escalates Labour Revolt Against Starmer

author: Josh Xiao
description: Russian leader Vladimir Putin will visit Beijing on May 20, the South China Morning Post reported, which would be days after President Xi Jinping’s summit in the Chinese capital with his US counterpart Donald Trump.
title: Putin to Visit Beijing Only Days After Trump Departs, SCMP Says

description: US President Donald Trump signaled China is willing to support negotiations with Iran, as he pushes for a diplomatic resolution to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Trump is visiting his Chinese counterpart President Xi Jinping in Beijing. Bloomberg's Stuart Livingstone-Wallace has more. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Says China Offered Help With Iran Negotiations

author: James Mayger
description: The Solomon Islands, a small Pacific nation caught in the China and US competition, elected a new prime minister seen as less friendly to Beijing than his predecessors.
title: China Skeptic to Lead Solomon Islands After Pact With Beijing

author: Anthony Halpin
description: Students at one of Russia’s leading engineering universities are getting a lucrative offer: ditch their studies for a year, fly drones for the military and earn more than 5 million rubles ($68,275) in pay as well as free tuition on their return.
title: Russia Presses College Students to Fill Ranks of Drone Pilots

author: Nectar Gan
description: Donald Trump met Xi Jinping in Beijing’s leadership compound on Friday, kickstarting a second day of talks that kept relations on an even keel but have yielded limited deals so far.
title: Trump and Xi Begin Second Day of Talks in Beijing’s Power Center

author: Heesu Lee
description: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi will meet in the South Korean city of Andong next week, extending a highly personalized diplomatic exchange at a time of shifting dynamics between the US and China, and mounting uncertainty over regional security.
title: Takaichi to Visit Korean President’s Hometown to Strengthen Ties

author: Keira Wright
description: Australia’s liquefied natural gas sector is facing the prospect of industrial action at major export operations, adding another supply risk for Asian buyers already scrambling for cargoes after disruptions in the Middle East.
title: Labor Unrest Threatens to Roil Australian LNG Export Projects

author: Daniel Carvalho
description: Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro denied that money he sought from a scandal-plagued banker was meant for his younger brother amid mounting pressure on his fledgling campaign.
title: Bolsonaro Says Scandal-Hit Banker Funds Weren’t for His Brother

author: Skylar Woodhouse
description: President Donald Trump said the US objective of recovering highly enriched uranium from Iran was “more for public relations than it is for anything else,” while reiterating his commitment to removing the nuclear material.
title: Trump Says He Wants Iran’s Uranium Mostly for ‘Public Relations’

author: Justin Sink, Skylar Woodhouse
description: US President Donald Trump said he raised the issue of granting Visa Inc. wider access to offer payments services to Chinese consumers and businesses during a meeting with Xi Jinping on Thursday in Beijing.
title: Trump Urges Xi to Allow Visa Access to China Payments Market

author: Yian Lee, Samson Ellis
description: Wealthy, democratic and strategically located off the Chinese coast, Taiwan has long been the most volatile issue between the US and China.
title: Why Taiwan Is the Hottest Issue Between the US and China

author: Ben Westcott
description: Soybean and corn futures gained as US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said China will make large purchases of American agricultural products, with President Donald Trump also emphasizing that the nation will look at “a lot of soybeans for our farmers.”
title: Soy, Corn Rise as US Says China to Buy More American Crops

author: Rakesh Sharma
description: Indian state fuel retailers raised prices of diesel and gasoline on Friday, the first hike in rates in four years, a move that will help tame demand and cut losses on fuel sales.
title: India Hikes Petrol, Diesel Prices for First Time in Four Years

author: Cliff Harvey Venzon
description: Tensions were already high Wednesday night in the Philippine Senate, days after lawmakers abruptly ousted its leader and an ex-cop wanted by the International Criminal Court showed up after six months in hiding.
title: 32 Gunshots Unleashed a Night of Chaos in the Philippine Senate

author: Catherine Lucey, Annmarie Hordern
description: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said he anticipates that China would commit to billions in American agricultural purchases, as Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping complete their summit in Beijing.
title: US Expects Dramatic Agricultural Purchases by China, Greer Says

description: Former Singaporean diplomat Kishore Mahbubani has argued for decades that the West misunderstands China’s rise. In this conversation he traces the story behind, and beyond, this week’s Trump-Xi talks. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Living With the Chinese ‘Tiger’

description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Melanie Hart, Atlantic Council Global China Hub Senior Director, discusses whether or not the meeting between President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping was successful. Representative Marlin Stutzman (R-IN), says China reopening to US beef is a "big deal" for farmers and calls President Trump's Beijing trip "one of the most consequential" of his presidency. Representative Jake Auchincloss (D-MA) says Xi Jinping is projecting confidence at the US-China summit and urges the US to “watch what he does” after President Trump said Xi would not send weapons to Iran. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump-Xi Talk Taiwan, Trade & Iran During Summit | Balance of Power: Late Edition 05/14/2026
